# Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Reese Delgado**
[Street Address]
[City], CO [ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield
Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-14**
- **Member:** Reese Delgado
- **Member ID:** W746473340
- **Reference number:** POC-13C871BB40-43334
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the prior authorization request for my lower back disc surgery (CPT 63030), which Anthem denied on 2026-08-14 under reference number POC-13C871BB40-43334. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file show a lengthy, supervised, and well-documented course of conservative care that meets the plan's own published requirements. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me.

Below I have set out the plan's own criteria, quoted from the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), and matched each one to what is in my records.

## 1. What the plan requires conservative management to include

The plan's guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records document exactly this combination:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 14 weeks, from 2026-04-11 to 2026-07-18, with 16 visits completed. This is recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary strategies (more than one):** NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23, which gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief.

That is physical therapy plus two additional conservative treatments — anti-inflammatory medication and an injection — aimed at reducing inflammation, relieving pain, and addressing the underlying problem.

## 2. Duration of conservative management

The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)"

and, for recurrent herniation:

> "Recurrent disc herniation when BOTH criteria are met: • Requirements for initial herniation • Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management"

My physical therapy alone ran 14 weeks, from 2026-04-11 to 2026-07-18. My NSAID trial ran 6 months. My symptoms have been present for 9 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest. Whichever of these measures is applied, the documented course is well beyond the six weeks the plan's guideline states.

## 3. Compliance with the plan of therapy

The guideline states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

and:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

I completed 16 physical therapy visits over 14 weeks and was discharged, with that course documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also completed the medication trial and the injection described above. This is a completed course for the current episode of care, not an abandoned or partial one.

## 4. Worsening or lack of improvement

The guideline states:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My records document 9 months of **progressive** pain that is unrelieved by rest, NSAIDs that gave inadequate relief over 6 months, and an injection that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief before the pain returned. I currently cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain going down into my right calf. That is the opposite of significant improvement after conservative care.

## 5. Pain and functional impairment

The guideline states:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and that I have radicular pain into my right calf. If a numeric pain score and an itemized list of affected daily activities are needed to complete this element, they are: [documented pain rating out of 10 from the chart] and [the specific ADLs/IADLs I am unable to perform, as documented by Dr. Okafor or the physical therapist]. I am asking that these chart entries be reviewed rather than treated as missing.

## 6. Imaging that correlates with the clinical findings

The guideline states:

> "Imaging studies. All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

and:

> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings"

My MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on 2026-06-22 — within six months of the request — and shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This matches my symptoms and exam precisely: radicular pain into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The imaging and the clinical picture point to the same level and the same side. The interpreting radiologist and facility are [name of interpreting radiologist and imaging facility, per the radiology report], and I ask that the full radiology report be reviewed.

## 7. Radicular findings

The guideline states:

> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:"

This sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of findings that I do not have a copy of, so I am not going to guess at what it contains. What my records show is radicular pain into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level of compression. If the specific listed findings are what the reviewer relied on, I ask that Anthem identify them so that my surgeon can address them directly.

## 8. Other criteria in the guideline

Several other provisions of the guideline appear in my denial file, including:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

> "Initial disc herniation when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

The first two of these end in colons and introduce lists of components and criteria that were not reproduced for me, so I will not attempt to restate them. On the third, my surgeon's evaluation and the diagnostic workup in my chart address the source of my pain; if Anthem believes a further source needs to be excluded, I ask that it say which one.

I also want to note, for completeness, that the guideline contains provisions under which the conservative care requirement does not apply:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when cauda equina syndrome or conus medullaris syndrome is present, and urgent intervention is indicated."

> "Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to cauda equina, lateral recess or foraminal compression (conservative management requirement waived)"

> "Acute neurologic deterioration including signs and symptoms of cauda equina syndrome, or rapid progression of neurologic deficits confirmed by imaging, regardless of underlying pathology."

I am not resting my appeal on these provisions, because I did complete conservative care. I raise them only because my imaging documents severe right lateral recess stenosis with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root and my exam documents a neurologic deficit at that level, and I would ask that Dr. Okafor's clinical judgment on the urgency of my situation be given weight.

## What I am asking for

The denial states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. Based on the plan's own published criteria, the records tell a different story: 14 weeks and 16 visits of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAIDs, a corticosteroid injection, no lasting improvement, and an MRI within six months that correlates with my exam findings.

I respectfully ask Anthem to:

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 63030 and approve the requested surgery;
2. If the denial is maintained, identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* that my records were found not to meet, including the items in the lists introduced by the provisions quoted above; and
3. Confirm the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who evaluated this request.

I am also requesting a free copy of all documents, records, and criteria that Anthem relied on in making this determination.

Per my denial notice, this appeal must be received by **2027-02-10**, which is within 180 days of the 2026-08-14 notice date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on that notice. I understand I can also manage this appeal at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card.

Enclosed with this letter: [list enclosures — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-07-18, MRI report dated 2026-06-22, office notes from Dr. Okafor, injection record dated 2026-05-23, medication history].

Thank you for taking a fresh look at my case.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Reese Delgado**
Member ID: W746473340
Date of birth: [DOB]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]

**cc:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
